samples.summary: Table-cell carried-child repaint (the `markDirty(cellInfo.tableBlockId)` branch) is never asserted
samples.evidence: The new `applyListLevelChanges` in editor.ts marks dirty via `layout.blockParentMap` and falls back to the enclosing table block for cell children (editor.ts ~1605). The only paint-level assertion in the suite is `describe('a carried child repaints at its new depth')` (line 439), which uses two top-level list items — `blockParentMap.get()` returns undefined there, so only the `?? change.block.id` half of the expression is exercised. The table-cell describe (lines 469-594) asserts stored model levels only (`cellLevels(store)`), which the diff's comment explicitly says cannot see a stale-cache repaint. If the tableBlockId fallback were dropped or wrong, a carried child inside a cell would repaint at its old depth with every model assertion still green.
searchedFor: grep fillText / paintedX usages in the test file

samples.summary: No test for a mixed (list-item + paragraph) selection through the now two-pass indent()/outdent()
samples.evidence: `indent()`/`outdent()` were split into `applyListLevelChanges(delta)` plus a second `forEachBlockInSelection` walk that early-returns on list items. Coverage is only single-kind: 'toolbar indent / outdent carry the subtree as well' (line 361) puts a bare caret on b1 so the paragraph b3 is never in the selection, and 'toolbar indent still moves a plain paragraph by marginLeft' (line 660) has no list items. The pre-existing mixed-selection test (line 239) presses Tab, which never touches marginLeft. So a regression where the second pass double-moves list items, or where the marginLeft pass stops running for a selection that also contains list items, would go undetected.

samples.summary: The cell-range (multi-cell) branch of `forEachBlockInSelection`, newly passing `cell.blocks` as siblings, has no list-level test
samples.evidence: Both walkers gained `fn(cellBlock, cell.blocks)` inside the cell-range branch (editor.ts ~1653, text-editor.ts ~2802), which is what keeps lists in different cells in separate planner groups. The new table describe only exercises a caret in one cell (line 518/542), a same-cell multi-block selection (line 560), and a body selection spanning the table (line 578) — none of these enters the `cellRange` branch. A wrong siblings argument there (e.g. passing the top-level array) would silently merge two cells' lists into one subtree context with no failing test.
searchedFor: grep _setSelectionForTest / cell-range helpers in the test file

samples.summary: Text-box coverage is a single indent/outdent/indent round trip with only the final state asserted
samples.evidence: The new text-box test (line 550) calls `api.indent(); api.outdent(); api.indent();` and asserts only the committed `[1, 2]` at the end. The round trip does constrain the behavior (a non-carrying outdent yields [1,3]), but no intermediate state is asserted, and the text-box surface has no coverage of the level-0 floor or the MAX_LIST_LEVEL ceiling as a subtree (those exist only as planner unit tests in test/model/list-level.test.ts). Also nothing asserts the layout cache is invalidated for the carried child in this surface.

samples.summary: `siblingsOf`'s `cell?.blocks ?? [block]` degenerate fallback is untested in both editors
samples.evidence: Both new `siblingsOf` helpers (editor.ts ~1620, text-editor.ts ~2879) fall back to a single-element array when the cell lookup misses. No test drives a stale/mismatched `blockParentMap` entry, so the fallback is never executed; a wrong fallback (e.g. returning `[]`) would make the gesture a silent no-op with no failing assertion. Low blast radius since the miss path should not occur in practice.
searchedFor: read the diff hunks for siblingsOf in editor.ts and text-editor.ts

samples.summary: No undo test over the new multi-block subtree edit
samples.evidence: `indent()`/`outdent()`/`handleListIndent` snapshot once and now write several blocks (parent plus carried children, possibly across cells). No test in the suite undoes the gesture and asserts every carried child returns to its original level; I searched editor-tab-bullet.test.ts and grepped listLevel across packages/docs/test and found no undo assertion tied to list levels. Failure would be user-visible (partial undo of an indent) but the single pre-walk snapshot makes it unlikely.

finding.summary: The new `markDirty` call in `applyListLevelChanges` (stale layout for un-selected children) has no test — every list-level test asserts only model `listLevel`, so the fix can regress silently
finding.evidence: The delta adds `markDirty(cellInfo?.tableBlockId ?? change.block.id)` in editor.ts:1604-1610 specifically because a child outside the selection was never marked dirty and "repaints at its old depth". The only tests touching this path are in packages/docs/test/view/editor-tab-bullet.test.ts: 'toolbar indent / outdent carry the subtree as well' (line 329) and 'a header list carries its children too' (line 345), plus editor-on-cursor-move.test.ts:225. All of them assert only `block.listLevel` / callback values read from the document model — they pass identically with the `markDirty` line removed, since the model write happens either way. Nothing asserts that the child block's cached layout lines were recomputed (the repo does have the tooling for this: incremental-layout.test.ts compares `lines` identity, and cursor-move-no-relayout.test.ts counts `measureText` calls through an OffscreenCanvas stub). So the user-visible symptom the fix targets — a nested bullet painted at its old indent after a toolbar Indent/Outdent — is untested and can ship again undetected.

verdict.reason: The claim is that the markDirty call in applyListLevelChanges has no test and that every list-level test asserts only model listLevel. That is false: packages/docs/test/view/editor-tab-bullet.test.ts:401-462 contains a dedicated describe block, 'a carried child repaints at its new depth', whose comment names the exact defect (indent()/outdent() only render(), so a carried child outside the selection must be marked dirty or its cached lines repaint at the old indent). The test (lines 439-461) records every fillText(text, x) via a canvas proxy (lines 24-71), stubs getBoundingClientRect so jsdom layout isn't collapsed (415-421), captures paintedX('child') after render(), then asserts after editor.indent() that the carried child's painted x is strictly greater (line 455) and after editor.outdent() that it returns to the original x (line 459). That is a paint-derived observable of the recomputed layout lines, not a model listLevel read, so it fails if the markDirty line is removed and the child's cached lines are reused (editor.ts:1527/1535 feed dirtyBlockIds into recomputeLayout; indent/outdent call render() synchronously at editor.ts:3584/3602 → 2252-2255). One meaningful test over the changed behavior exists, so the absence claim is refuted.

searchedFor: Grep siblingsOf across repo (only src/view/editor.ts, src/view/text-editor.ts)
finding.summary: New table-cell sibling resolution (`siblingsOf`, and `fn(cellBlock, cell.blocks)`) has no test at all
finding.evidence: The diff adds `siblingsOf()` in both editor.ts (~line 1614) and text-editor.ts (~line 2862), plus passes `cell.blocks` from the cell-range, same-cell and table-walk branches of `forEachBlockInSelection`. Subtree detection is entirely driven by which array is handed in, so a wrong array silently re-levels the wrong blocks (e.g. cursor in a cell but siblings resolved to top-level blocks). Nothing exercises it: the new specs in test/view/editor-tab-bullet.test.ts use only flat top-level list items (no `table`/`tableData` fixture anywhere in that file), the new unit test test/model/list-level.test.ts feeds synthetic arrays directly and never goes through the editor, and grep for `siblingsOf` matches only the two src files — no test references it. No test in packages/docs/test indents a list nested inside a table cell.

verdict.reason: The finding's central factual claim is false. packages/docs/test/view/editor-tab-bullet.test.ts contains a dedicated describe('list level inside a table cell') block (lines 464-594) with a real tableData fixture (setupTable, :480-510) mounted through the real initialize() editor and a real MemDocStore - the logic under test is not mocked. Four tests cover every branch the new sibling resolution feeds: (1) :518-540 puts a cursor-only caret in cell block c1 and calls editor.indent(), which is exactly the fn(block, siblingsOf(block, cellInfo)) path at editor.ts:1712; (2) :542-558 drives the same through a real keydown (pressIndentKey), hitting the text-editor.ts:2863/2870 siblingsOf; (3) :560-576 covers the same-cell multi-block branch that hands cell.blocks (editor.ts:1678); (4) :578-593 covers the body-selection table-walk branch fn(cellBlock, cell.blocks) (editor.ts:1697). Assertions read the STORED post-edit levels out of blocks[1].tableData.rows[0].cells[0].blocks (cellLevels, :513-516) and assert exact tuples such as [1,2,0] / [1,2,1], plus store.getDocument().blocks[2].listLevel === 0 - which pins precisely the failure mode the finding claims is unguarded (siblings resolved to top-level blocks instead of the cell array). Those assertions would fail if the wrong array were handed in, so this is meaningful, non-vacuous coverage. siblingsOf not appearing in any test file is expected: it is a private closure in editor.ts/text-editor.ts, correctly exercised through its public entry points (indent/outdent, Tab, Cmd+]).
